title: Reading fluency rubric (example)
subject: Language
notes: An example rubric to show the format. It is not an official curriculum or assessment: adapt the levels to your class.

levels.label: Beginning
levels.descriptor: Reads many words wrongly; meaning is lost.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Reads most common words; stumbles on new ones.

levels.label: Secure
levels.descriptor: Reads nearly all words correctly; corrects own slips.

levels.label: Strong
levels.descriptor: Reads all words correctly, including new ones.

levels.label: Beginning
levels.descriptor: Reads word by word, with long pauses.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Reads slowly, in short bursts.

levels.label: Secure
levels.descriptor: Reads at an even, comfortable pace.

levels.label: Strong
levels.descriptor: Reads at a natural pace, as if speaking.

levels.label: Beginning
levels.descriptor: Ignores full stops and commas.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Notices some full stops.

levels.label: Secure
levels.descriptor: Pauses at most full stops and commas.

levels.label: Strong
levels.descriptor: Groups words into meaningful phrases.

levels.label: Beginning
levels.descriptor: Flat voice throughout.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Some change in voice.

levels.label: Secure
levels.descriptor: Voice matches most of the text.

levels.label: Strong
levels.descriptor: Voice brings characters and mood to life.

levels.label: Beginning
levels.descriptor: Cannot say what the text was about.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Recalls a few details, out of order.

levels.label: Secure
levels.descriptor: Retells the main events in order.

levels.label: Strong
levels.descriptor: Retells events and explains why they happened.
